summary: One passes-cluster fixup to PULPHardwareLoops.cpp. B01 and B02 are handled in one commit because both come from the same place: computeCount did not implement Hexagon's comparison-dependent count. The fix restores Hexagon's latch negation, declines EQ-continue loops, uses Hexagon's imm/imm path, adds the equality/ceil adjustment, ports the upstream 89adc2d4f93b runtime distance check as an SLT/SLTU mask guard (on the first compared value, so a wrapping first step is also exact), and leaves the guard out when a dominating branch proves the distance. loopCountMayWrapOrUnderFlow is re-enabled and ported for != loops (constants via checkForImmediate, range checks read from branches since RISC-V has no analyzeCompare, a dominating Start!=End proof accepted first). BGEU/COND_GEU are now unsigned. The fork's $x0 COPY is kept as it was, so unchanged loops get identical code. Pre-existing defect from fork commit f1b7aebff8c2.

other_errors_seen: Pre-existing, not fixed: seed 27 (hwloop-fuzz) O2/O3 MISMATCH on baseline and fix alike. Tail duplication leaves two lp.setup in two predecessors of one loop (F003 reviewer's finding).

Missed optimisation from this change: 7 of 2292 fuzzer hardware loops are no longer formed (seeds 10,17,111,138,214). They are != loops whose start could equal the end value unless you reason past the dominating guard, e.g. (m&3)!=0 implies m!=0. The re-enabled wrap check declines them. Unguarded do{}while(--u!=0) is declined for the same reason. LSR drops nsw/nuw from the IV update, so no-wrap flags cannot be used.

Limit, same as Hexagon: a count of 2^32 cannot be represented. An ordered loop whose IV would pass the type's max (End within step of INT_MAX/UINT_MAX) is not exact; that is UB for signed C and an endless loop for unsigned.
Pre-existing sweep TU failures, unrelated and identical on the baseline: k05/k06/k07/k10 -file TUs and k10b (front-end errors: v2h argument type, AT_L2_EVENT, __builtin_pulp_add2div2).

proposed_test.content: The F003 reviewer IR shapes (logs/20-F003-review/ge.ll: ge0, gem, eqhdr; shapes.ll: eqm, ne0, eq0exit), plus an unguarded do{}while(--i>=0) with a register bound and an unsigned (i+=2)<m loop. Generate the checks with update_llc_test_checks.py. Key checks: ge0 -> 'addi aN, a1, 1' then 'lp.setup x0, aN'; gem -> 'sub' + 'addi 1' + lp.setup; eqm/eqhdr -> no lp.setup; the unguarded loops -> slt/sltu, neg, and, addi 1 in front of lp.setup.
